heading: Liji 3 · Wang Zhi 王制 · Royal Regulations · Wang Zhi I.1 … Wang Zhi II.10
Liji 3 · Wang Zhi 王制 · Royal Regulations · Wang Zhi IV.4 … Wang Zhi IV.16
Liji 3 · Wang Zhi 王制 · Royal Regulations · Wang Zhi III.11 … Wang Zhi IV.3

items.text: Nourish your aged parents to complete filial piety.
items.quote: nourished the aged, to secure the completion of filial piety

items.text: Show pity to orphans and solitaries; do not neglect those bereaved.
items.quote: showed pity to orphans and solitaries, to reach those who had been bereaved

items.text: Give places according to age when the aged are assembled.
items.quote: there was a feast, when places were given according to age.

items.text: Honor your rulers and love your superiors.
items.quote: honoured their rulers, and loved their superiors.

items.text: Do not seek ground set apart for graves for any other purpose.
items.quote: Ground set apart for graves could not be sought (for any other purpose).

heading: Liji 3 · Wang Zhi 王制 · Royal Regulations · Wang Zhi II.25 … Wang Zhi III.10

items.text: Observe three years of mourning for your father and mother, and let no other business interfere with those rites.
items.quote: The mourning rites of three years (for parents) extended from the son of Heaven to all... no other business should interfere with the rites of mourning.

items.text: Present the seasonal offerings to your ancestors in your principal apartment: scallions in spring, wheat in summer, millet in autumn, and unhulled rice in winter.
items.quote: The common people, in the spring, presented scallions; in summer, wheat; in autumn, millet; and in winter, rice unhulled.
items.conflict: Offerings and worship belong to God alone; the dead do not receive food.

items.text: If you are a son by a concubine, do not preside over the ancestral sacrifices.
items.quote: A son by a concubine did not (preside at) the sacrifices.
items.conflict: Concubinage and exclusion from leading worship because of one's mother are contrary to Scripture.

items.text: Do not let your house and its apartments surpass the ancestral temple.
items.quote: The house and its apartments did not surpass the ancestral temple.
items.conflict: We need not maintain an ancestral temple; God alone is to be worshiped, not ancestors.

heading: Liji 3 · Wang Zhi 王制 · Royal Regulations · Wang Zhi II.11 … Wang Zhi II.24

items.text: Keep the proper order of the ancestral temple observances and do not neglect them.
items.quote: Where there had been neglect of the proper order in the observances of the ancestral temple, it was held to show a want of filial piety
items.conflict: Offering such rites to ancestors conflicts with worshiping God alone (Exodus 20:3-5).

items.text: Before going forth, offer the Zhào sacrifice in your father's fane.
items.quote: and the Zhâo in the fane of his father.
items.conflict: Ancestor offerings are not acceptable Christian worship; the dead cannot be honored by such rites (Deuteronomy 18:10-12).

items.text: Before a punitive expedition, receive your charge from your ancestors and the plan from the college.
items.quote: He had received his charge from his ancestors, and the complete (plan) for the execution of it in the college.
items.conflict: Seeking guidance from the dead is forbidden; God alone directs His people (Deuteronomy 18:10-12).

items.text: After a punitive expedition, return and announce to your ancestors what you have done.
items.quote: on his return he set forth in the college his offerings, and announced (to his ancestors) how he had questioned (his prisoners), and cut off the cars (of the slain).
items.conflict: The dead are not a heavenly court to report to; worship and thanksgiving belong to God alone (Deuteronomy 18:10-12).

items.text: When the inspection tour is finished, repair to the ancestral temple and offer a bull in each fane from your high ancestor to your father.
items.quote: he returned (to the capital), repaired (to the ancestral temple) and offered a bull in each of the fanes, from that of his (high) ancestor to that of his father.
items.conflict: Offering bulls to the dead contradicts Christ's once-for-all sacrifice (Hebrews 10:10-12).

heading: Liji 3 · Wang Zhi 王制 · Royal Regulations · Wang Zhi V.28

items.text: Fulfill a father's duty to your son.
items.quote: the duties between father and son

items.text: Fulfill a son's duty to your father.
items.quote: the duties between father and son

items.text: Fulfill an elder brother's duty to your younger brother.
items.quote: elder brother and younger

items.text: Fulfill a younger brother's duty to your elder brother.
items.quote: elder brother and younger

items.text: Fulfill a husband's duty to your wife.
items.quote: husband and wife

items.text: Fulfill a wife's duty to your husband.
items.quote: husband and wife

items.text: Fulfill the duty of the old to the young.
items.quote: old and young

items.text: Fulfill the duty of the young to the old.
items.quote: old and young

heading: Liji 3 · Wang Zhi 王制 · Royal Regulations · Wang Zhi V.12 … Wang Zhi V.27

items.text: When your father is eighty, let one son be free from public duties to wait on him; when he is ninety, let the whole family be freed.
items.quote: Where (an officer) was eighty, one of his sons was free from all duties of government service; where he was ninety, all the members of his family were set free.

items.text: Mourn your father and mother for three years.
items.quote: Parties mourning for their parents had a discharge for three years.

items.text: Give the fatherless orphan a regular allowance; he has no one to tell his wants.
items.quote: One who, while quite young, lost his father was called an orphan... they all received regular allowances.

items.text: Give a regular allowance to an old man who has lost his sons; he has no one to tell his wants.
items.quote: an old man who had lost his sons was called a solitary... they all received regular allowances.

items.text: Give a regular allowance to an old widower who has lost his wife.
items.quote: An old man who had lost his wife was called a pitiable (widower)... they all received regular allowances.

items.text: Give a regular allowance to an old widow who has lost her husband.
items.quote: an old woman who had lost her husband was called a poor (widow)... they all received regular allowances.

items.text: On the road keep behind a man of your father's years or an elder brother; if carrying a burden with an elder, take the heavier load.
items.quote: A man kept behind another who had a father's years; ... both were borne by the younger; and if the two were too heavy for one, he took the heavier.

items.text: Do not borrow vessels for ancestral sacrifice; make them before making anything for your own private use.
items.quote: nor to make vessels for his own private use before he had made those for sacrifice.
items.conflict: Ancestral sacrifices conflict with the first commandment and Christ's finished sacrifice.
